name: BN6's hit flag by a chip's icon element
why: As a chip is used BN6's engine ORs into its attack element (MegaMan's AttackVars +2, his AI data +0xA2) a hit flag by its record's icon element (Sword 0x80, Cursor 0x40, Wind 0x20, Break 0x10: the table at 0x080129E4), which BN6's hit pass acts on (a Break breaks a guard, a Sword is a sword); BN5's chip use writes the element alone. BN6's engine rule for every chip, BN5's among them (docs/multirom/one-net.md: the chips' finer calls); the flag is the one the chip in use (his AttackVars +0x14) has by its icon element, BN6's record's or, for a chip of the registry's own, its BN5 record's as BN6's (src/core/xchips_record.c).
evidence: BN6 0x0801271E-0x08012728 (the chip's numbers written for its attack, 0x080126E4): ldrb r1,[r6,#4]; ldrb r2,[r6,#6]; ldr r0,=0x080129E4; ldrb r0,[r0,r2]; orrs r1,r0; strb r1,[r7,#2]
BN5 0x0800FEA4-0x0800FEA6 (its twin, 0x0800FE6A): ldrb r1,[r6,#4]; strb r1,[r7,#2]
the table's 16 bytes: 00 00 00 00 00 80 40 00 20 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 (icon element 5 Sword, 6 Cursor, 8 Wind, 9 Break)
chip_sword: MegaMan's +0xA2 0 in BN5's and 0x80 in BN6's from the Sword's use (t32) on
